title: Can Borussia Dortmund finally end their title wait? Three big questions for Bundesliga leaders
summary: Niko Kovac’s team lead the way and, with Bayern Munich wounded, have a golden chance to be German champions for the first time in 15 years Borussia Dortmund dreams have a habit of becoming nightmares, like when they somehow handed Bayern Munich the Bundesliga title on the final day of the 2022-23 season. Or when an 89th-minute Arjen Robben goal won the 2013 Champions League final for the same opponents. Whenever Dortmund suffer heartbreak, it usually involves Bayern. As things stand, however, Niko Kovac’s side hold a two-point lead over Bayern at the top of the Bundesliga. Both teams are unbeaten, but Dortmund may be the more stable of the two at the moment, especially with Harry Kane expected to miss several months through injury. Continue reading...

title: Bills, Eagles and Bears pull off last-gasp wins in trio of Thanksgiving thrillers
summary: Bass hits from 57 yards at the gun to lift Buffalo Elliott’s 59-yarder caps Eagles’ 21-point comeback Bears take NFC North lead on Odunze’s late catch Tyler Bass hit a 57-yard field goal as time expired to give the Buffalo Bills a 13-10 victory over the Kansas City Chiefs on a rainy, windy Thursday night. The Bills improved their AFC-leading record to 10-1. James Cook rushed for 117 yards and scored on a five-yard run. Bass also hit a 54-yard field goal in the defensive struggle. Continue reading...

title: ‘It’s not helping’: calls for guardrails and regulations as AI use rises at US retailers
summary: Labor leaders and advocates urge protections for workers and consumers as AI use becomes more commonplace As millions of Americans begin holiday shopping this Black Friday, consumers and workers alike are already seeing how artificial intelligence is reshaping the retail landscape. Anna, a cashier in a southern Oregon Walmart and leader with United for Respect, who requested to remain anonymous for fear of retaliation, criticized the implementation of AI at Walmart and its effects on workers. title: Heavy rain, wind and flooding hit much of US on Thanksgiving
summary: Homes left without power and holiday travel disrupted as storms pound east coast and other parts of the US Storms have flooded communities in the US east coast, knocking out power to nearly a million customers and prompting the first-ever postponement of Macy’s Thanksgiving Day parade in New York City. High winds and flooding hammered both coasts, disrupting holiday travel. More than 900,000 homes and businesses were without electricity on Thursday evening, with the majority in east coast states, according to the outage tracking website PowerOutage.us. More than 2,200 flights to or from US destinations were delayed and more than 400 were cancelled, according to the flight tracking service FlightAware. Continue reading...
